rationale: The question is how well three adaptations are delivered, whom they reach and whether completion improves in routine care, which is an implementation question. RE-AIM structures the measures (reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, maintenance) and CFIR structures conversations with people who leave. The adaptations are introduced in sequence so that each can be observed. Nothing was retrieved, so the decision rests on the confirmed empty search and the investigator's local facts, not on ledger claims.
alternatives: Cluster randomised comparison of adapted and standard groups (refused: about ten groups a year cannot give a useful comparison, and the question is about routine delivery)
Study of people who leave early without adaptations (refused: the clinic plans the changes anyway and needs to learn from them)
Before-after comparison of completion only (refused: misses reach, fidelity and reasons for leaving)
whyNotMoreComplex: A randomised or stepped wedge comparison would need several clinics; one clinic's cohorts can show whether reach and completion move and why, which is what the clinic has to decide.

decision.statement: Introduce the orientation call and the hybrid video option in the first 2027 groups, and the evening group once staff hours are approved, as a RE-AIM guided implementation study with follow-up of people who leave.
decision.question: How should the clinic introduce and evaluate the three adaptations to the group programme?

criteria.text: Completion of six or more sessions stays at or below 41 percent in the first two adapted groups.
People who leave can be reached for a brief outcome check at three months.

gates.requirement: Clinic manager approval to move physiotherapist and psychologist hours to one evening a week in 2027
Research ethics board determination of whether the evaluation needs full review

alternatives: Study of people who leave early without adaptations
decision.note: No ledger claim exists because the recorded search returned no records; the decision rests on the confirmed empty search and the investigator's local facts. Both gates are unknown.

summary: Implementation study recommended; the decision cites no claims and is blocked by two unknown gates.
